headline: Biological foundation models face scrutiny on mutation effects, toxicity and attribution
label: Biological Foundation Model Evaluation
summary: Recent benchmarks and frameworks test whether protein and genome language models generalize beyond their training distributions and evolutionary priors.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a shift from reporting model performance toward testing what these models actually learn. PFArena benchmarks protein language models, LLMs and LLM-based agents on single- and multi-mutant modification tasks, while the VenusREM-Harness training-free method fuses protein foundation model scores with MSA and structural evidence for fitness prediction. Evaluation scrutiny extends to genome models: the phage stress test finds weak, covariate-explained predictive signal for Evo2 against MS2 and ΦX174 mutation data. Other items address explainability, including EFT tracing explanations during training across four TCR-epitope models and GAMA attribution for generative sequence models trained on positive-only data. Criteria for molecular foundation model generality, transferability and out-of-distribution generalization are also proposed. Newer directions include agentic mechanistic world modelling (gemot) and a perspective on moving from zero-shot likelihoods to experimental supervision.
